reason: The text contains only three explicitly named characters: God (יְהוָה), Moses (מֹשֶׁה), and Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה). All other references to groups—such as 'children of Israel' (בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), 'Egyptians' (מִצְרַיִם), 'army,' 'chariots,' and 'horsemen'—are collective nouns rather than named individual characters. Each of the three named characters holds a leadership role: God as the supreme authority issuing commands, Moses as the leader of the Israelites, and Pharaoh as the king of Egypt. No non-leadership figures are named in this passage.
